Recent findings suggest that A total of 11 VUS/CCOP variants (AAC ≥ 10) had absolute effect sizes exceeding 7.99 cm, with P values ranging from 1.6 × 10−4 to 1.1 × 10−31 (five with P < 1.75 × 10−9; Fig. 4 and Supplementary Table 20). Three are NPR2 missense variants classified as VUSs in ClinVar but with large effects on height in our study (between −8.24 and −9.53 cm). Although none of these missense variants achieved genome-wide significance, two (p.G221R and p.R921Q) are experimentally validated loss-of-function variants44. Here we highlight large-effect variants lacking clear clinical annotations (either unannotated or classified as VUSs/CCOPs) that exemplify how population-scale association analyses provide relevant data that clinical geneticists can use to evaluate potentially disease-causing variants.

We undertook an exome-wide association study in 1,450,633 individuals, identifying 207 height-associated genes after conditioning on common variants—115 more than an earlier large-scale sequencing study9. In 17 genes, singleton pLoFs—the rarest and most deleterious variant class—were associated with absolute effects on height 52× larger than the average common variant (8.92 cm versus 0.17 cm). Although we noted substantial overlap with Mendelian syndromes, fewer than 25% (44 out of 207) of genes include a stature or skeletal growth component in their OMIM description2, and only 16% of height-increasing genes (9 out of 57) are both included in OMIM and annotated with stature or skeletal growth phenotypes. Collectively, rare variant associations demonstrated strong concordance with genes implicated by common variant associations and reflected established biological processes influencing height, including growth factor signalling, extracellular matrix organization and transcriptional regulation.

According to recent reports, our results illustrate classic trade-offs in genetic association studies between effect size and allele frequency. Expanding from singletons to low-frequency variants up to 1%, and from pLoFs to missense variants, increased the number of implicated genes from 17 to 179 but greatly diminished the average absolute effect size. Tests that more explicitly accommodate effect size heterogeneity12 or small proportions of causal variants11 within each gene increased gene discovery another 16%, bringing the total to 207 genes. As no single analysis captured all of the implicated genes, we maximized gene discovery by combining gene-based P values from multiple models using a well-calibrated omnibus gene-based test10.

It has been revealed that the genes we found to be associated with height include those in well-understood pathways but also implicate potentially new areas of height biology. For example, in the GH/IGF pathway, growth hormone (GH1) signals for IGF1 production, stimulating skeletal growth through cartilage generation in the growth plate45. While Mendelian syndromes with altered stature as a major feature are linked to eight members of the GH/IGF pathway—GH1, GHR, GHRHR, GHSR, IGF1, IGF1R, IGFLAS and PAPPA2 (ref. 46)—our results include seven of these eight (Supplementary Table 23), and implicate three others (PAPPA, STC2 and GHRH). Furthermore, for several genes that were previously considered to have autosomal recessive modes of inheritance (GHRHR, IGFALS, IGF1 and PAPPA2), our results show that loss-of-function and deleterious missense variants have apparent effects in the heterozygous state (Supplementary Table 23). Finally, while GH1–IGF1 is generally considered the major driver of post-natal growth and development, the IGF2 pathway is believed to act mainly during prenatal development with uncertain effects on adult height47. Human genetic evidence for a role of the IGF2 pathway in height has previously been limited to extreme short stature (>3 s.d. below average) in Silver–Russell syndrome, caused by disruptions in the IGF2 gene itself (although not implicated here)48. Our results include association in an additional IGF2 pathway gene: IGF2BP2 through singleton pLoFs (β = −8.67 cm, P = 1.52 × 10−10; Table 1), an mRNA-binding protein that stabilizes IGF2 mRNA, providing additional evidence for a developmental role of IGF signalling in adult height.

Accurate complex trait prediction is a key aspiration of human genetics. Current prediction efforts focus on common variants with effects that are individually small but substantial in aggregate. Supplementing this approach by adding both rare variants with individually large effects and burden tests provides substantial predictive value for carriers. Among 337 carriers across our 17 singleton pLoF genes, adding rare variant effects to common variant prediction models improved the prediction performance to nearly that of common variants in the full population (R2 = 0.72 in carriers versus 0.73 across the full sample). However, as these variants are so rare (<0.1% of individuals), this has a limited impact at the population level.

In a recent development, FGFR3 and PTPN11 frequently arose as interesting case studies throughout this work. First, they represent the unusual case in which rare missense variants collectively yielded a significant burden association with no contribution from pLoFs. They reduce height through GoF mechanisms22 and are known causes of achondroplasia7 and Noonan syndrome23, respectively. However, their burden effects were relatively modest (3–15× smaller; −2.31 cm for FGFR3; −4.12 cm for PTPN11) compared with the effects of a few individual variants: −29.8 cm effect for FGFR3 p.G380R; −14.2 cm for PTPN11 p.N308D; and −12.2 cm for PTPN11 p.R265Q. For most other genes, the effect sizes were more consistent for missense and pLoFs and combining them yielded the most statistically powerful analysis.

Sources indicate that collectively, this work substantially expands the breadth of rare genetic associations for adult height. Beyond directly implicating 207 genes, we demonstrate how rare variant gene discovery at scale can bridge the gap between common variant GWAS and Mendelian disease genetics, providing valuable data for identifying functional genes and interpreting observed variation in clinical settings.

Our discovery analysis comprised six exome-sequenced cohorts jointly called on an Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT) modified xGen exome capture from the RGC-ME study49: the glaucoma-ascertained African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study III (ADAGES; n = 1,941)50; the Mexico City Prospective Study (MCPS; n = 138,667), comprising residents from the Iztapalapa and Coyoacán districts of Mexico City35; the population-based UK Biobank (UKB; n = 452,583); and three health-system cohorts: Mount Sinai BioMe Biobank (BioMe; n = 26,850), Geisinger Health System DiscovEHR (GHS; n = 165,080)51 and Penn Medicine BioBank (PMBB; n = 40,945)52.

We performed a meta-analysis across six replication cohorts not part of the RGC-ME49. Four cohorts were exome sequenced using a TWIST capture: the household-based prospective ‘BangladEsh Longitudinal Investigation of Emerging Vascular and nonvascular Events’ (BELIEVE; n = 53,830) Study53 and three hospital-based cohorts: The Biobank at Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine (CCPM; n = 48,799)54, Mayo Clinic Project Generation (n = 72,472) and University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) at LA Study (ATLAS) Precision Health Biobank (UCLA ATLAS; n = 38,406). The longitudinal All of Us (AoU) research programme was whole-genome sequenced; participant-level phenotypic and genetic data cannot be removed from the trusted research environment and we therefore did not use AoU data for prediction analyses (AoU; n = 381,888)55. The prospective, population-based Malmö Diet and Cancer Study (MDCS; n = 29,172) was exome sequenced by IDT exome capture but could not be jointly called in the RGC-ME due to regulatory restrictions.

We calculated an individual’s standing height by first converting all height measurements to centimetres, removing measurements <75 cm or taken before age 18, and then taking the median across the remaining height measurements. We excluded individuals for whom their genetically predicted sex differed from their self-reported sex as well as 76 bone marrow transplant recipients for whom their DNA was collected from blood. Within each cohort, we applied rank inverse normal transformation separately for each sex and used this rank inverse normal transformed height phenotype in genetic association analyses. To approximate height effect sizes in centimetres, we multiplied effect sizes (in s.d. units) by 7.994 cm, the sex-stratified, sample-size-weighted s.d. in the discovery cohorts.

All genomic data analysed here was generated as previous described9,49,55. In brief, exome capture was performed using IDT (ADAGES III, BioMe, GHS, MCPS, MDCS, PMBB and UKB) or TWIST (BELIEVE, CCPM, Mayo Clinic, UCLA ATLAS) capture reagents, sequencing was performed on the Illumina HiSeq 2500 or NovaSeq 6000 system, and sequencing reads were aligned to GRCh38. AoU used DNA extracted at the Mayo Clinic (blood or saliva) and sequenced at Baylor College of Medicine, Broad Institute, or University of Washington: sequencing centre and DNA source were included as batch covariates55 (Supplementary Fig. 9). PLINK (v.1.9)56 converted the pVCF to PLINK files for downstream analyses. Quality control included sample/variant missingness of <10%, ±10 bp buffer window around target regions, heterozygosity Hardy–Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE) P > 1 × 10−100, excess heterozygosity HWE P > 1 × 10−30 and setting male heterozygous genotypes in the non-pseudoautosomal region (non-PAR) of chromosome X to missing using the PLINK256 option --set-hh-missing. We implemented a previously described support vector machine (SVM)-based quality control protocol to identify likely artefactual variants9 and then used these predictions to create individual-level covariates for GWAS.

Variant Effect Predictor (VEP)57 v.100.4 (Ensembl58 release 100) annotated variants on human protein-coding transcripts and assigned a single consequence per variant based on the canonical transcript defined using MANE58, APPRIS59 and Ensembl canonical tags as previously described58.

We used REGENIE’s60 linear whole-genome regression test to perform three genetic analyses on chromosomes 1–22 and X in the discovery: (1) a TOPMed61 imputed common variant GWAS (AAF > 0.01; n = 19,527,870 variants); (2) a rare variant exome analysis (AAF ≤ 0.01, AAC ≥ 10; n = 9,086,709 variants excluding those tested in the imputed variant GWAS); and (3) a gene-based association analysis of rare coding variation (n = 19,107 gene-level omnibus tests). We set a single unified Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold of P < 1.75 × 10−9 across all three analyses, accounting for all common, rare and gene-based tests performed (0.05/28,633,686 tests). A discussion of calibration in these results is provided in the Supplementary Note.

According to recent reports, for the non-PARs of chromosome X, we assumed a dosage-compensation model in which homozygous reference male individuals are coded as 0 and hemizygous male individuals are coded as 2 (and heterozygous male individuals were set to missing). In step 1 of REGENIE (that is, prediction of individual trait values based on genetic data), we included genotyped variants with an AAF > 1%, <10% missingness, HWE P > 10−15 and linkage-disequilibrium (LD) pruning (1,000 variant windows, 100 variant sliding windows and an r2 threshold of 0.1). The covariates used in REGENIE steps 1 and 2 are described in Supplementary Table 24.

It has been revealed that to identify conditionally independent common GWAS variants, we performed an iterative conditional meta-analysis using REGENIE’s leave-only-same-chromosome-in (LOSCI) option on TOPMed-imputed dosage data. LOSCI conditions the variant/gene being tested only on the same-chromosome variants to avoid model overfitting. In each iteration, distance-based clumping (1 Mb minimum) identified the lead variant (P < 1.75 × 10−9), which became covariates in subsequent iterations. After 22 iterations, no variants reached significance (P < 1.75 × 10−9), yielding 3,034 independent variants used to condition all rare variant and gene-based association tests (REGENIE’s model includes each variant individually).

REGENIE collapses qualified (based on AAF and annotation) rare coding variants by gene and assigning each individual’s genotype as the maximum of their alternate alleles (2 for individuals who are homozygous alternate carriers for a qualified variant; 1 for heterozygous carriers of any qualified variant; and 0 for individuals who are homozygous reference for all qualifying variants). Burden tests were performed on these genotypes whereby effect sizes represent the per-allele effect of carrying a qualified variant. pLoFs comprised frameshift, stop gain, splice-donor or splice-acceptor variants. Missense variants were evaluated using six in silico predictors: ESM-1v62, SIFT63, PolyPhen2+HumDiv64, PolyPhen2+HumVar64, MutationTaster65 and LRT66. Variants were selected for inclusion in burden tests based on AAF, status as pLoF and—for missense variants—how many algorithms predicted the variant to be deleterious. Missense variants were classified as deleterious if predicted pathogenic by ESM-1v (using a threshold of 0.78) or all five other algorithms; and possibly deleterious if predicted to be not pathogenic by ESM-1v but predicted to be pathogenic by 1–4 other algorithms. Burden tests were then performed using every combination of five different AAF thresholds (singleton (4.17 × 10−7), 0.0001, 0.001, 0.005 and 0.01) and 7 different combinations of variant class: (1) pLoF; (2) pLoF + deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (3) pLoF + at least possibly deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (4) pLoF + all missense + stop lost + start lost; (5) deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; (6) at least possibly deleterious missense + stop lost + start lost; and (7) all missense + stop lost + start lost—yielding 35 burden tests.

To properly adjust for multiple correlated tests across a large number of genes, we used gene-P10, an omnibus gene-based test framework that uses ACAT67 to combine P values from four complementary rare variant gene-based tests—BURDEN-ACAT10, Sparse Burden Association Test (SBAT)10, SKAT-O12 and ACAT-V11—into a single P value per gene (Supplementary Fig. 1) as previously described10. After identifying genes associated through gene-P, we quantified the number of significant associations from these four underlying tests (Extended Data Fig. 1a). We classified genes into two groups: burden-associated (P < 1.75 × 10−9 in BURDEN-ACAT or SBAT) or non-burden-associated (P < 1.75 × 10−9 in ACAT-V or SKAT-O and P ≥ 1.75 × 10−9 in both BURDEN-ACAT and SBAT).

Sources indicate that we used a previously described method for genetic ancestry assignment49. In brief, using a diverse reference panel comprising 11,354 individuals from 95 populations, we calculated the proportion of haplotype sharing of each sample and assigned them to one of six genetic ancestries (African (AFR), Indigenous American (AMR), East Asian (EAS), European (EUR), Middle Eastern (MEA), and South Asian (SAS)) if they had greater than 50% of that genetic ancestry; those with no majority ancestry were assigned to an ‘OTH’ group. We recognize that these commonly used labels oversimplify an individual’s genetic, cultural and environmental diversity, and use them only out of convenience to properly adjust association tests for genetic ancestry.

Sources indicate that in both imputed and sequenced data, we assigned each variant a single AAF representing the maximum AAF across six fine-scale ancestries. On the basis of the fine-scale ancestry maximum AAF, we classified variants as common (AAF ≥ 1%; n = 19,514,636 in imputed data with INFO ≥ 0.3 in all discovery cohorts) or rare (AAF < 1%; n = 44,600,231 in exome data). When a variant was rare (<1%) in the exome, but common in the imputed data (≥1%), we classified them as common (n = 335,522). Singletons in the discovery analysis were defined as those with only a single AAC for variants on chromosomes 1–22 and the X chromosome’s PAR, and a single hemizygous or heterozygous genotype in the X chromosome’s non-PAR. REGENIE used these AAFs and singleton definitions when writing burden test genotypes and running the gene-based tests (options --aaf-file and --set-singleton). For replication analyses, we used the same AAFs as in the discovery analysis but included an additional 12,777,247 unique variants in the replication data. Singletons in the replication comprised variants that were either (1) a singleton in the discovery or (2) a singleton in the replication that was absent from the discovery.

We compared the pLoF burden effect sizes to common variants identified by GWAS at the same genes by linking conditionally independent GWAS variants to their nearest gene through genomic distance. For genes with multiple nearby GWAS variants, we computed the mean absolute GWAS effect size. For each gene g with kg GWAS loci (where kg > 0), we computed the ratio of the singleton absolute pLoF effect size to the GWAS conditional joint effect size. Specifically, for gene g with singleton pLoF absolute effect size |\({{\beta }}_{g}^{\mathrm{pLoF}}\)| and a set of GWAS conditional joint effect sizes \({\beta }_{1}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), \({\beta }_{2}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), … , \({\beta }_{{k}_{g}}^{\mathrm{GWAS}}\), we defined the per-gene ratio as:.

Industry observers note that these ratios quantify the fold-increase in phenotypic effect conferred by complete gene disruption (through a singleton pLoF carried by an individual) relative to the effect of common regulatory or coding variation at the same locus identified through GWAS. Ratios of >1 indicate that the singleton pLoF has a larger effect on height than the nearby common GWAS variant, consistent with the expectation that rare, gene-disrupting variants tend to have larger per-allele effect sizes than common variants due to stronger purifying selection.

Recent findings suggest that we built a common variant PGS using PLINK56 from 3,039 common (Supplementary Table 8) variants from two sources: first, 3,034 conditionally independent common variants identified through iterative conditional meta-analysis (Methods and Supplementary Table 2) and second, five common variants identified from the exome and not tested with imputed data. The common variant PGS was computed as a weighted sum of alternate alleles, where the magnitude and direction of the weight was based on the estimated variant effect size (in s.d. units) from a joint model in the discovery (n = 826,066; Supplementary Table 1) of all 3,039 variants (Supplementary Table 8) and the same covariates (Supplementary Table 24) used in the association analyses (Supplementary Note).

In a recent development, we constructed four versions of rare variant PGS (rvPGS), based on the 179 genes with a significant gene-P and either a significant BURDEN-ACAT or SBAT test, weighted using s.d. effect sizes: (1) rvPGSSNP: all 77 significant (P < 1.75 × 10−9, AAC ≥ 10) rare variants in these genes (after LD clumping for variants with R2 < 0.2), weighted by the single-variant effect size; (2) rvPGSpLoF: all 179 pLoF (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size; (3) rvPGSmissense: all 179 deleterious missense (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size; and (4) rvPGSsynonymous: all 179 synonymous (AAF < 1%, AAC ≥ 10) burden associations weighted by effect size. When predicting height based on both rvPGSSNP and burden-based rvPGS, both the burden genotypes and burden effect sizes were recomputed to exclude the variants included in the single-variant rvPGS to enforce independence between the rvPGS.

Industry observers note that all estimations of variance explained by the PGS were performed using genes and effect sizes from the discovery (n = 826,066) but estimated using the replication (n = 242,679 excluding AoU; Supplementary Table 1). First, for each cohort–sex combination (five cohorts × two sexes), a linear regression model was fit of height (in centimetres) on the covariates used in the replication association tests. The PGS of interest was added into the model, and the variance explained was calculated as the difference in adjusted R2 between the two nested models. The reported value was the mean of the ten cohort–sex subsets (five cohorts × two sexes). When computing variance explained by rare-variant PGS, the null model included the 3,039 common variant PGSs (Supplementary Table 8) in addition to covariates (Supplementary Table 24) mentioned above.

In replication cohorts (n = 242,679; excluding AoU; Supplementary Table 1), we predicted an individual’s height (in centimetres) from a mean-centred common variant PGS in s.d. units as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that where \({\bar{\mathrm{height}}}_{\mathrm{cohort},\mathrm{sex}}\) and \({\text{s.d.}}_{\mathrm{cohort},\mathrm{sex}}\) are the mean and s.d. of height among replication individuals matched on cohort and sex.

Although height differs by genetic ancestry, we did not stratify predictions explicitly by genetic ancestry to avoid excluding small subpopulations (Supplementary Table 1). However, most replication cohorts (excluding AoU) comprised individuals of a single genetic ancestry, so stratification by cohort was effectively the same as stratifying by genetic ancestry.

To predict an individual’s height using rare variants, we calculated various rvPGS using the 179 gene-P genes with significant burden-ACAT or SBAT P value. Owing to the nested nature of burden tests with respect to AAF (for example, a burden test of <1% AAF variants also includes all the variants in a singleton burden test), we restricted to only selecting a specific AAF for each class of variants. We also ensured that in any predictive models including both burden and significant single variants, the burden effects were recomputed without any significant single variants. rvPGS tested include: pLoF AAF < 1%, deleterious missense AAF < 1%, all significant rare variants, height predictions incorporating rare variant PGS (rvPGS) were calculated as:.

To assess the accuracy of any PGS, we report the R2 of a univariate linear model of predicted height on observed height.

In a recent development, the Loss-of-function observed/expected upper bound fraction (LOEUF) metric follows a uniform distribution18 and was available for 201 out of 207 gene-P genes (all but FGD1, HDAC6, IRS4, NRK, SCMH1 and SHOX). We considered genes to be LoF-constrained if they were in the first LOEUF quintile. When comparing whether two gene sets significantly differed with respect to LOEUF, we used a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on LOEUF ranks.

To assess whether height-associated genes identified through rare variant burden testing were enriched for biologically relevant annotations—OMIM disease genes (all and stature/skeletal growth-related, curated in ref. 2), constrained genes and nearest gene to a GWAS signal—we used two-sided Fisher’s exact tests to test for enrichment; when odds ratios were infinite due to zero count cells, we applied a continuity correction of +1 to all cells.

To address potential confounding by coding sequence (CDS) length, whereby longer genes may be more likely to contain rare qualifying variants and reach significance, we performed a canonical CDS-length-matched enrichment analysis. For each gene, we identified the five closest background genes by canonical CDS length, sampled without replacement, to construct a null set and repeated all analyses described above using these CDS-matched background genes.

It has been revealed that we used a two-sided 2 × 2 Fisher’s exact test to assess whether individuals carrying rare variants were more likely to be observed in the subset of the population based on various thresholds (in s.d. units) of either their predictive error (that is, the absolute difference in the observed and common-variant predicted height; Supplementary Table 18) or their observed height (Supplementary Table 19). The set of genes that we examined included either genes with a significant (P < 1.75 × 10−9) burden test (for example, 17 genes from singleton pLoF burden tests, 8 genes from singleton deleterious burden tests; Fig. 1b and Supplementary Table 6) or all significant gene-P genes with a significant SBAT or burden-ACAT test (Fig. 1d and Supplementary Table 4). While varying the variant class, AAF threshold, gene set and s.d. threshold, we kept the comparison group constant, defaulting to <0.5 s.d. from the mean.

According to recent reports, when comparing height association results to ClinVar, height association statistics from the meta-analysis of the discovery and replication cohorts (n = 1.45 million) were used to maximize sample size. For consistency, the list of gene-P genes used for subsetting variants was the list of 207 genes from the discovery only (Supplementary Table 4). ClinVar data were downloaded in July 2025. To subset for diseases with a stature-related component, the union of three filters was used:.

String matching of ClinVar disease column for any of the following strings: stature, height or chondroplasia.

Searching for any of the following manually curated, height-related Human Phenotype Ontology terms in the list of observed phenotype codes: HP:0004322, HP:0003510, HP:0001519, HP:0003498, HP:0003508, HP:0008909, HP:0003502, HP:0008845, HP:0008857, HP:0008848, HP:0011405, HP:0011406, HP:0011404, HP:0011407, HP:0000098, HP:0008873, HP:0003521, HP:0008921, HP:0008922, HP:0008929, HP:0008905, HP:0000002.

Searching the observed phenotype codes for 506 height-related MONDO terms (Supplementary Table 25). This list was generated by MONDO label, definition and synonym fields for the strings stature, height and chondroplasia, and removing any field with the string normal stature.

Any ClinVar entry meeting at least one of these criteria was included in the analysis, yielding 47,763 variants before filtering for those in gene-P genes. While not comprehensive (several variants in Supplementary Table 21 affect known height genes but are not included), this list identifies a set of variants in ClinVar for which the listed diseases are confidently determined to involve stature. Enrichment testing for significant variants in each ClinVar pathogenicity bin (Supplementary Table 22) was performed using the binomial test (probability of success = 1.75 × 10−9).

The UCLA IRB (17-001013) approved patient recruitment and sample collection for UCLA’s Precision Health Activities. Lund University’s Regional Ethics Committee approved the Malmö Diet and Cancer Study. ADAGES III approval and consent was provided by each institution’s IRB. The AoU IRB follows the regulations and guidance of the NIH Office for Human Research Protections for all studies, ensuring that the rights and welfare of research participants are overseen and protected uniformly.

Further information on research design is available in the Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary linked to this article.

Summary statistics from discovery analyses are available at Figshare68 (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34056885). The following data resources are available by application: All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset Release 8 (https://www.researchallofus.org/), BELIEVE study (https://believestudy-bangladesh.org/accessing-believe-data/), BioMe (https://mountsinaimillion.org/en/contact), CCPM (https://medschool.cuanschutz.edu/cobiobank/contact-us), GHS (https://regeneron.envisionpharma.com/vt_regeneron/), Project Generation Mayo Clinic Biobank (https://www.mayo.edu/research/centers-programs/mayo-clinic-biobank/for-researchers), MDCS (https://www.malmo-kohorter.lu.se/malmo-cohorts), PMBB (https://pmbb.med.upenn.edu/contact.php) and UK Biobank (http://www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/register-apply/). Data from the MCPS are available to researchers on application. The MCPS Data Sample Sharing policy is available in English and Spanish at https://www.ctsu.ox.ac.uk/research/mcps; metadata describing the available datasets can be examined through the Data Showcase (https://datashare.ndph.ox.ac.uk/mexico); and MCPS ancestry-specific allele frequencies are available at https://rgc-mcps.regeneron.com. Privacy regulations prohibit individual-level UCLA-ATLAS data from being published, although processed data and summary statistics are available in the Supplementary Tables or through the UCLA-ATLAS browser (https://atlas-phewas.mednet.ucla.edu). Genetic variation for all discovery cohorts (ADAGES III, BioMe, GHS, MCPS, PMBB, UKB) are made publicly available through the RGC Million Exome Browser (https://rgc-research.regeneron.com/me/home). The list of 12,111 COJO SNPs and 462 OMIM height and skeletal growth-related genes were downloaded from supplementary tables 10 and 11 of ref. 2, respectively (https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-022-05275-y/MediaObjects/41586_2022_5275_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx). GIANT GWAS summary statistics were downloaded from the Broad Institute: (https://giant-consortium.web.broadinstitute.org/index.php/GIANT_consortium_data_files#2022_GWAS_Summary_Statistics_and_Polygenic_Score_.28PGS.29_Weights). LOEUF scores (gnomAD v.4.1) for constraint were downloaded from the Broad Institute (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/downloads). ClinVar annotations were downloaded in July 2025 (https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/).

We used the following software: Burden heritability regression (v.0.5.0-alpha; https://github.com/ajaynadig/bhr), ComplexHeatmap (v.2.20.0; https://github.com/jokergoo/ComplexHeatmap), DeepVariant (v.0.10; https://github.com/google/deepvariant), METAL (v.2020-05-05; https://github.com/statgen/METAL), Minimac4 (v.1.01; https://github.com/statgen/Minimac4), PLINK (v.1.90b6.21 and v2.00a3LM; https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink2/), REGENIE (v.4.1; https://github.com/rgcgithub/regenie), TOPMed Imputation Server (release-3; https://imputation.biodatacatalyst.nhlbi.nih.gov/#!), VEP (v.100.4; https://github.com/Ensembl/ensembl-vep/).

Industry observers note that a, UpSet plot decomposing the 207 genes identified by gene-P into the four underlying gene-based test methods: SBAT, BURDEN-ACAT, SKAT-O, or ACAT-V. The union of SBAT and BURDEN-ACAT yielded 179 genes which we defined as burden genes. UpSet plots for the 179 burden genes broken down by (b) variant class and (c) AAF threshold.

Industry observers note that forty-one variants with AAF < 0.01% are shown. The dashed black line indicates no effect, and the solid red line indicates the burden effect size when aggregating all the variants in the figure (β = −3.1 cm).

Each point represents a group of burden tests of a given type (specified by colour) that meet a given P-value threshold. Proportion of negative synonymous burden tests with P < 1.75×10−9 (n < 5) not shown. Two-sided burden P-values were calculated by REGENIE. Point estimates represent observed proportions and error bars represent 95% confidence intervals around these estimates. Vertical bars indicate the number of genes included in each estimate.

Industry observers note that estimated using burden heritability regression (BHR) in discovery data (n = 826,066 individuals). Point estimates represent the mean cumulative heritability estimates for each variant annotation and frequency range. Error bars represent 95% confidence intervals around these point estimates.

According to recent reports, variance explained is calculated as the difference in adjusted R2 between nested linear models of height: one with only common variants and covariates and one that also includes a rare variant PGS. Each point represents all burden tests of a given type (specified by colour) that meet the given P-value threshold (the number of burden tests in each point is given in Extended Data Fig. 3). Two-sided burden association statistics were calculated by REGENIE. Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) used to determine whether the variance explained by rare variant burden tests was significantly different from zero at a conservative, Bonferroni-corrected α=0.0001 to adjust for 500 tests performed.

In a recent development, solid vertical lines represent mean values for each prediction method; black dashed line indicates no difference between observed and predicted height. All individuals shown are in replication data.

Variants (AAF < 0.1%) are separated by ClinVar pathogenicity. Black dashed lines indicate a Z-score of 0 and red dashed lines indicate the Z-score threshold corresponding to P = 1.75×10−9 (Z = ± 6.02). Two-sided single-variant association statistics were calculated by REGENIE. Red numbers represent the number of variants with Z scores more extreme than the genome-wide threshold.

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:09.

Premier League clubs are reportedly interested in signing Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown during the January transfer window.

The 24-year-old has followed in the footsteps of Jude Bellingham and Jobe Bellingham in recent years, leaving the English domestic scene to forge a successful football career on the continent.

Brown has been a regular appearance-maker for the Turkish giants this season and played the full 90 minutes on Wednesday night, when the Turkish Super Lig club beat Shakhtar Donetsk in the Champions League.

With his performances catching the eye in Europe this term, Fenerbahce man Brown is supposedly admired by a number of high-profile clubs, including Nottingham Forest of the Premier League.

The highlight of the youngster's season so far undoubtedly arrived on November 4 when he found the net and provided an assist during the Yellow Canaries' 3-2 Champions League success over Liverpool.

According to German transfer specialist Florian Plettenberg, Fenerbahce defender Brown is attracting interest from across the continent following an impressive opening to the 2026-27 season.

The report claims that a number of Premier League clubs are keen on bringing the 24-year-old back to English shores, with the winter transfer window opening at the turn of the calendar year on January 1.

Providing encouragement for those sides eyeing up a swoop for Brown, the left-back supposedly has a release clause totalling £19.2m in his current contract with the Super Lig powerhouses.

It is understood that the stipulation can be triggered either during the upcoming January or summer transfer windows, meaning that potential suitors have options in their hunt for the player.

Since a 2-1 home defeat by Goztepe on October 31, Brown and Fenerbahce have strung together a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1), a streak which includes that historic home success over Liverpool.

Brown spent a large chunk of his academy time within the ranks of East Midlands club Derby County, making 27 appearances for their Under-21s side before commencing his professional career abroad.

The 23-year-old started at Swiss outfit Lausanne in the Swiss Super League following a switch in June 2021, playing 43 matches and scoring five goals across a two-year stint at Stade de la Tuiliere.

The former Rams youngsters truly made a name for himself at Belgium side Gent before securing a high-profile transfer to Turkish and European giants Fenerbahce during the summer of 2025.

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery mentioned: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Recent findings suggest that villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'.

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 11:30.

FC Cincinnati play host to Nashville SC on Saturday night looking to book their place in the conference semi-finals of the MLS Cup playoffs.

The home side hold a 1-0 advantage in the best-of-three tie having earned a surprise victory on away soil in the opening fixture.

Having booked their place in the MLS Cup playoffs as far back as September 19, the assumption was that Nashville SC would have too much quality for FC Cincinnati, who finished the regular Eastern Conference campaign with 31 fewer points.

Nashville had also defeated Cincinnati in the final game of the regular season by a 2-0 scoreline on away territory.

Nevertheless, an early own goal from Nashville midfielder Patrick Yazbek gave Cincinnati a 1-0 victory at Geodis Park on November 22.

That marked Nashville's first defeat since September 10, ending a 10-match unbeaten streak that featured seven wins and three draws.

It has been revealed that B. J. Callaghan will have concerns that their efforts throughout 2026 are close to going to waste, with Nashville having failed to score in two of their last four matches.

However, Nashville make the trip to the TQL Stadium on a five-game unbeaten run on their travels, while just 11 goals were conceded in 17 regular season away contests.

As far as Cincinnati are concerned, they netted 39 goals from the same amount of home matches, the third best attacking return in home fixtures in the Eastern Conference.

Despite finishing down in ninth place, 10 points came from their closing five fixtures, and Pat Noonan's team have now emerged victorious from five of their last seven games, albeit only losing to Nashville in this exact fixture on November 7.

Prior to the first leg, Cincinnati had the benefit of shaking off a lack of match sharpness through registering a 3-1 win at Orlando City SC in the Eastern Conference wildcard tie.

Nashville SC Major League Soccer form:.

Former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia is an option to replace Bryan Ramirez at left wing-back for FC Cincinnati.

Tom Barlow, with 10 goals and five assists during the regular season, may also be introduced into the final third, but Noonan is not expected to overly-tinker with a winning team.

Meanwhile, Jack Maher could be brought into the Nashville SC backline after Maxwell Woledzi suffered an injury during the second half of the last game.

Yazbek and Bryan Acosta are battling for one place in central midfield, while Warren Madrigal may be recalled on the flank.

Sam Surridge, who has netted 21 league goals this season, has scored five times in his last seven appearances.

FC Cincinnati possible starting lineup:.

Celentano; Doudera, Malatini, Robinson, Smith, Malacia; Martinez, Gidi; Nwobodo; Evander, Denkey.

Nashville SC possible starting lineup:.

Schwake; Najar, Maher, Palacios, Baker-Whiting; Yazbek, Corcoran; Espinoza, Mukhtar, Saad; Surridge.

Although FC Cincinnati will be confident of making home territory count, we can only anticipate an improved performance from the Eastern Conference regular season winners. With that in mind, Nashville could edge this fixture by the odd goal in three to take the tie to a decider.

BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (380 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.
  • The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW stated.

The main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the manufacturer sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic remarked his company would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have unveiled intends to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has confirmed that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler announced on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the firm statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, revealed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

  • The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 11:46, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 11:48.

Palmeiras and Estudiantes meet on Saturday afternoon in the 2026 Copa Libertadores final.

The clash at the iconic Estadio Centenario revives memories of the 1968 final, when Estudiantes claimed the first of their four titles and became the first Argentine side to beat a Brazilian team in the final.

Palmeiras, meanwhile, are chasing a fourth continental title after reaching three of the last six finals.

After 58 years, Palmeiras have the chance to renew their rivalry with Estudiantes in a final worthy of the occasion. The 1968 final was decided over three matches: the Argentines won the first leg in La Plata before losing at the old Pacaembu.

In the decider at the same Estadio Centenario, Estudiantes won 2-0, with goals from Ribaudo and Juan Ramon Veron. One of the goals in Estudiantes’ first Libertadores triumph was scored by the father of the club’s current president, Juan Sebastian Veron.

Palmeiras have not been as dominant in 2026 as in previous years. They drew two of their six group-stage matches, but have taken the lead in eight of their last 10 continental fixtures during the knockout rounds.

In the round of 16, the Alviverde gained revenge on Cerro Porteno, completing a quartet of meetings between the sides this campaign.

According to recent reports, abel Ferreira's men then needed penalties to overcome LDU Quito in the quarter-finals and Fluminense in the semi-finals. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel proved crucial on both occasions, making three saves in total.

After losing the national title to Flamengo last Saturday, Palmeiras fielded a reserve side in Tuesday’s visit to Chapecoense and suffered a 3-0 defeat.

Recent findings suggest that although the result did not change their position in the Brasileiro table, Palmeiras are now winless in four matches across all competitions. They have also conceded in each of their last five outings.

Like Palmeiras, Estudiantes have also faced the same opponent four times in this edition: Flamengo, the reigning continental champions and two-time Brazilian champions.

In a recent development, in Group A, Alexander Medina's men suffered a narrow defeat at the Maracana and drew 1-1 at the Jorge Luis Hirschi. In the semi-finals, the Pincha held the favourites to two goalless draws before goalkeeper Fernando Muslera starred in the shootout, saving penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paqueta, and Bruno Henrique.

That trademark Argentine resilience was also evident against Universidad Catolica in Chile, and especially across the two quarter-final matches against Corinthians.

Estudiantes have conceded an average of just 0.5 goals per match across their last 10 Libertadores games. Since the round of 16, Muslera has been beaten only twice.

According to recent reports, their main concern is at the other end: Estudiantes have scored no more than once in nine of their last 10 matches in the tournament. A closely fought contest in Montevideo could therefore be in prospect.

Palmeiras Copa Libertadores form:.

Palmeiras’ medical staff are racing to get defender Murilo fit after he sustained a left-thigh injury. If he is unavailable, Bruno Fuchs is expected to join captain Gustavo Gomez and Alexander Barboza in the back three, ahead of youngster Luis Benedetti.

Forward Paulinho is also a major doubt after developing inflammation in the muscle and bone tissue in his calf. Even if he recovers, he could miss the Copa do Brasil final.

Uruguay international full-back Joaquin Piquerez was rested against Rubro-Negro but is expected to return on the left in his home country.

Fellow full-back Jefte remains provisionally suspended pending a hearing before the Anti-Doping Sports Justice Tribunal (TJD-AD).

For Estudiantes, former Sao Paulo midfielder Gabriel Neves is still recovering from a fractured arm and is likely to miss out.

Neves joins midfielder Baltasar Rodriguez, who is suspended after being sent off in the second leg of the semi-final.

Joaquin Correa sustained a grade-two muscle injury to his right thigh against Talleres on November 7.

With the usual recovery period around three weeks, the former Botafogo forward is undergoing intensive treatment in a bid to make the bench.

Palmeiras possible starting lineup:.

Miguel; Gomez, Murilo, Barboza; Giay, Freitas, Pereira, Piquerez; Arias, Roque, Lopez.

Estudiantes possible starting lineup:.

Muslera; Mancuso, Nunez, Palacios, Rojo; Piovi, Burgos, Castro, Palacios, Cetre; Carrillo.

With two solid, well-organised defences and goalkeepers in good form, a high-scoring contest seems unlikely.

Palmeiras may dominate possession, but Estudiantes could respond with a set-piece goal if they fall behind.

If the final goes to penalties, Muslera could have the chance to redeem himself after a difficult World Cup.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 17:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:54 EST, 24 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has left the door open for a return to Sporting Lisbon amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Manchester United.

Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.

The United captain has become equally popular at Old Trafford, but returned to Lisbon on Tuesday night with a question mark hanging over his next move after talks over a new contract stalled.

Fernandes’ current deal is due to run out at the end of June – and he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January 1 – although United are expected to trigger an automatic 12-month extension to prevent him from leaving as a free agent in the summer.

Asked if he would consider a move back to the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where United meet Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Fernandes remarked: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.

‘Sporting was the first club that believed in my potential. I’ve always felt here from the fans – regardless of what may have happened – all the love and kindness from them, and that was essential to make me grow as a player.’.

Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a fresh contract to extend his stay at Man United.

On his future at Old Trafford, Fernandes insisted that he wants to focus on turning United’s season around after they slipped into the relegation zone and replaced head coach Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

It has been revealed that ‘We have time to speak about that,’ stated Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.

‘Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games, and then we can talk about a contract. Now is not the moment.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards.
  • "Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.
  • Recent findings suggest that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that on November 4, 2001, London's Leicester Square became a world of witches and wizards. The occasion was the world premiere of "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" (released in the US and India as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone").

"Thousands of excited fans, some dressed up in wizard hats and cloaks, gathered to catch a glimpse of arriving celebrities," the BBC reported at the time.

Recent findings suggest that daniel Radcliffe, who played Harry Potter, was just 12 years old and clearly impressed by the spectacle. The BBC quoted him as saying, "It is so cool. I have never heard my name shouted so much in an hour.".

The crowds highlighted just how far Harry Potter fever had spread in only four years.

The first Harry Potter book was published by Britain's Bloomsbury in June 1997, with an initial print run of just 500 hardcover copies.

About 5,000 paperback copies were also released around the same time.

It has been revealed that today, first editions are prized collectors' items, with hardcover copies commanding high prices at auction. In mid-October, one sold for $400,000 through US auction house Heritage Auctions.

In a recent development, at first, the book's popularity grew largely by word of mouth among schoolchildren. Media attention followed when it won the prestigious Nestle Smarties Book Prize later that year.

With an estimated 120 million-plus copies sold worldwide, it is the best-selling book in the series and ranks among the best-selling novels of all time.

For years, J.K. Rowling's public image was defined by her extraordinary rise from a single mother on welfare to a billionaire.

In a recent development, but in recent years, debate over her views on gender and transgender identity has increasingly overshadowed that success. It's an issue Rowling herself frequently weighs in on.

In an essay published on her website on October 21, 2026, Rowling reiterated her opposition to what she calls the "current, dominant strain of trans activism." She argues that this movement "holds that a man who declares himself a woman is, literally, a woman, and is therefore entitled to be treated as a woman in all contexts." Rowling argues that allowing trans women into single-sex spaces poses a risk. She describes biological sex as an indisputable biological fact.

Such statements have led critics to accuse Rowling of transphobia, while others regard her stance as a defense of women's rights and safety.

The controversy has also divided her fans. Some stand by Rowling, while others try to draw a distinction between the books and their author.

It has been revealed that others have left Harry Potter behind altogether. One former fan is German YouTuber Coldmirror, known for her Harry Potter parodies. The media artist from the Bremen area, whose real name is Kathrin Fricke, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper: "I don't have any love left for Harry. I'm still somewhat interested, but I can no longer watch it in good conscience." She cited Rowling's campaigning against transgender people as the reason.

Recent findings suggest that the "Harry Potter" film cast is divided as well. The three main stars — Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint — have publicly spoken out in support of transgender people. Meanwhile, Ralph Fiennes, who played Lord Voldemort, and Helena Bonham Carter, who portrayed Bellatrix Lestrange, have defended Rowling's right to express her views.

Industry observers note that despite the controversy surrounding Rowling, Warner Bros., which holds the Harry Potter film rights, is bringing the books back to the screen — this time as a series for HBO. The premiere is scheduled for December 25.

Industry observers note that the eight-episode first season is an an adaption of the first book. Even though the episode lengths haven't been revealed, the scope of a TV series gives each book much more room than the original films did. That means more time to explore subplots, character development and everyday life at Hogwarts. While many fans are looking forward to a more detailed adaptation, others remain skeptical. They find it hard to imagine the familiar characters being played by anyone else.

The upcoming trio consists of Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley.

It has been revealed that J.K. Rowling is an executive producer on the show. HBO states, however, that her views on gender identity won't be reflected in the storyline. Several people involved in the new production have publicly distanced themselves from her views. Paapa Essiedu, who has been cast as Severus Snape, signed an open letter supporting transgender people. Rowling subsequently noted she had neither the power nor the desire to have him removed from the show because of it. John Lithgow, who plays Dumbledore, and Nick Frost, who portrays Hagrid, have also spoken out against Rowling's views.

Meanwhile, the Harry Potter merchandising machine is still going strong. On November 4, Britain's largest Harry Potter store to date is set to open in London. According to Warner Bros., the two-story shop covers more than 1,950 square meters.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 11:46.

Aiming to move themselves back into the top half of the Championship, struggling West Ham United welcome promotion-chasing Stoke City to the London Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Hammers' woeful run of form continued at the Fratton Park base of Portsmouth earlier in the week, whilst the Potters picked up yet another Staffordshire victory, this time at the expense of Millwall.

Back in the Championship for the first time since 2012, West Ham United were expected by many to sit at the top of the rankings and waltz to a Premier League return, however, the East Londoners hit a latest low on Tuesday night.

The Hammers extended their winless run to a worrying six matches (D2 L4) at Fratton Park, where a first-half effort from Odin Bailey was enough for Portsmouth victory, with the visitors once again failing to break down a stubborn second-tier defence.

Since the early-November arrival of Scott Parker to the managerial hotseat, West Ham have collected just two points across a quartet of fixtures, dropping down to 13th spot in the Championship table - a staggering 11 points behind first-placed Middlesbrough.

Following three away matches in their past four, the Hammers are back at their London Stadium base on Saturday, when Parker's men will be looking to halt a five-game winless run (D2 L3) at the East London venue.

In fact, West Ham rank 17th in terms of home form so far this season, with the pre-season title favourites last picking up three points in front of their own supporters on September 11, when Wrexham were hit for six without reply.

After placing between 16th and 18th in each of the past four Championship seasons, Stoke City have swapped midtable mediocrity for a Premier League chase in 2026-27, winning 11 of their past 14 league fixtures.

The in-form Potters have now gone seven games (W6 D1) without defeat after Wednesday night's impressive showing against Millwall, with George Hirst grabbing the headlines once again courtesy of a game-winning brace.

After recording five consecutive league victories for the first time since the days of Tony Pulis in February 2008, Stoke have moved up to second spot in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Middlesbrough.

The Staffordshire side managed just six league wins on the road last season but could equal that tally already with success this weekend at the London Stadium, where the Potters last played in April 2018.

That East London clash represents the most recent meeting between West Ham and Stoke, with a 90th-minute leveller from towering striker Andy Carroll forcing a share of the spoils following Peter Crouch's opener.

West Ham United Championship form:.

Looking for his first victory as West Ham boss at the fifth attempt, head coach Parker could make changes from the side that was defeated by Portsmouth.

However, there is little room for manoeuvre at right-back, where Joel Veltman should start in the absence of Kyle Walker-Peters (muscle).

Young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick could play once again, with Danish stopper Mads Hermansen dropped to the bench for the past two games.

Stoke suffered a major injury blow during the win over Birmingham City last weekend, with Djibril Soumare picking up a muscular injury.

In the absence of the influential midfielder, Jack McGlynn could start in a deeper role alongside fellow summer arrival Ethan Galbraith.

West Ham United possible starting lineup:.

Herrick; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Mayers; Soucek; Bowen, Engels, Mukasa, Solomon; Piroe.

Stoke City possible starting lineup:.

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, McGlynn, Galbraith, Devenny; Manhoef, Bae, Hirst.

Without a victory under upcoming boss Parker, West Ham's ambitions of an instant Premier League return are fading promptly.

Stoke will be in the mood to take full advantage of a Hammers side devoid of confidence, however, we feel that a share of the points is forthcoming at the London Stadium.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.
  • It has been revealed that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

It has been revealed that this young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

According to recent reports, ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

Industry observers note that iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola mentioned. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha stated to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

Industry observers note that iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

The floodgates are opening ⚽️ Florian Wirtz scores his first goal of the season for Liverpool 🇩🇪 https://t.co/5HP72tA3bE.

In a recent development, iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

Industry observers note that “They are so good on the ball,” Iraola remarked of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

A moment to forget for Virgil van Dijk 😨 Georges Mikautadze takes full advantage to give Villarreal the lead at Anfield 🟡⚽️ https://t.co/3JTl00UwYa.

Recent findings suggest that the pace of the game was slow and Villarreal were in control until the later stages of the half. Koumas and Cody Gakpo created a chance and from the corner that resulted Mac Allister headed in Tsimikas’s cross. Liverpool were up and running. Ngumoha’s cross from the left was unwisely left by Cardona for Araújo to score and the game was level.

Out of nowhere 😳 Ronald Araújo sneaks in to grab Liverpool's equaliser on the stroke of half-time 🇺🇾 https://t.co/Qrn8PmB2bJ.

Then came Ngumoha’s major second half, creating the third for Mac Allister. The teenager went past Cardona and the substitute Juan Foyth in a couple of strides. Wirtz dispatched the fourth from Gakpo’s ball.

According to recent reports, even so there was still time for Liverpool to show that they had sacrificed some defensive stability. The absence of a right-back cost them when substitute Tani Oluwaseyi ran into that area of the pitch to score Villarreal’s third late on. The third win of Liverpool’s Champions League season puts them second in the 36-team super-table, and behind defending champions Paris St-Germain only on goal difference.

Liverpool are also seeing a upcoming star emerge. Ngumoha might be the most expensive academy signing in the game’s modern history but alongside the £100m men he looks like a risk that was worth taking.

We have said all night about momentum, and talking about how they Liverpool will play against Brighton at the weekend, I’ll be amazed if Rio [Ngumoha] doesn’t start because of the momentum that he has got from this game.

You see the fans, you see how everyone got a lift by him and that’s what they need at the weekend, they need someone to lift them.

They are flying. Their confidence is through the roof. A similar style to Villarreal. They are second in everything after Barcelona. It has been a good game to prepare and we will use it.

I am really happy with Rio. He is trying to improve everything and we are trying to correct things. He played a lot on the left and know he is playing a lot on the right and he has adapted really well. We encourage him always. Even defensively as well he is improving. He has become a more complete player – and we must not forget he is 18!

In a recent development, rio Ngumoha was magnificent tonight. Such a threat, and he dedicated himself to his tasks. On the ball this kid has so much potential, and I say kid, but he’s a young man. He has so much quality and it’s stuff that you can’t teach to be honest.

Sources indicate that what he does with the ball at his feet, that is God given ability, and his hard work on the training pitch, doing things day in and day out, and being ruthless, is what he said in his interview, and I like that. He wants to be decisive, and I love that about him.

I’m not tall but I love going in the box. I really like it. They know I like to attack the near post. I scored in the World Cup as well. It was a good header. The second goal, Rio, was amazing. I talk with him about cutting it back on the floor.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not something I really practice. My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it’s something I got from him.

Last year was a really difficult year for all of us. It was clear I was not at the level and I am the first one to say. Something wasn’t right in the group and this manager changed it. The way we play is different, I don’t like to compare. I’m feeling good.

A lot of things happened today. They were much better than us in the first half and we were much better in the second half. When we’ve been under pressure, we answered well. When we relaxed, we made mistakes. You cannot relax against very good opposition. I value the win.

We have to know that if we don’t go to the limit, it will be difficult. We are facing very good teams. It’s good to come back but we’ve started losing too many goals this season.

Florian Wirtz has scored or assisted in three consecutive games for the first time in his Liverpool career: 🅰️ vs LASK 🅰️ vs Brentford ⚽️ vs Villarreal https://t.co/woLWk2SGGL.

Recent findings suggest that it was a top performance from the boys. We were two goals down but the mentality was always there. We knew we were going to win.

According to recent reports, it’s up there with one of the best I’ve played. I enjoyed myself and the team helped me a lot.

Industry observers note that whenever I get the ball and there’s an opportunity to go one v one or two v one, I believe in myself. I’ll just keep going and be ruthless.

Rio Ngumoha talking to Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime: “Definitely one of the best games I played. I enjoyed it. Whenever I get the ball and go one v one, the more it makes the opposition worried.”.

When he was reminded that he was the youngest Englishman to provide an assist in the Champions League, he said: “Records are amazing to break.”.

Industry observers note that and on playing on the right instead of the left wing: “It’s helped me a lot in training. Slowly I’m getting better on the right.”.

And to hear the crowd chanting his name: “This stadium, we have the best fans. To hear my name being chanted is a dream.”.

PSG’s 4-2 win over Barcelona tonight also puts them on nine points. Aston Villa, Arsenal, Real Madrid, Sporting and Real Betis are the teams playing tomorrow night with the opportunity to maintain a 100 per cent record.

Nine points from a possible nine for Liverpool in the Champions League, but they made hard work of it. Some dysfunction was probably to be expected after Iraola decided to start without Mac Allister, Isak, Wirtz and Barcola, but their defensive structure was unzipped far too easily at times.

Recent findings suggest that on the other hand, they dragged themselves off the canvas and the night belonged to Rio Ngumoha. He looked dangerous every time he received the ball, set up the third goal, and received a standing ovation when he was substituted. Liverpool need to put that contract in front of him sharpish.

Still time for another hairy moment at the back for Liverpool, but Perez’ shot from the edge of the area is blocked and that will surely be that.

Industry observers note that pape Gueye floats a cross straight down the throat of Alisson. A wasted opportunity for Villarreal. But still a couple of minutes to play.

Just the three minutes of added time to play, and Liverpool are probably grateful for that.

Could Liverpool be in for a nervous finish? Their defence is caught square again after a run in behind from Ayoze Perez, and Oluwaseyi was totally unmarked at the back post to apply a simple finish at silence Anfield.

Cody Gakpo threatens to score Liverpool’s fifth with an overhead free-kick, teed up by McConnell’s chipped cross to the back post, but he could not keep the attempt down.

The game is meandering towards its conclusion now, though a Villarreal goal would make things interesting.

Another Liverpool youngster enjoys a taste of first-team actions: James McConnell is on for Nyoni.
