In a recent development, perez hits the post for Villarreal with only Alisson to beat, but the flag is raised for offside. I think that would have stood had he found the net, Van Dijk may have been playing him just onside.

Ngumoha receives his standing ovation, lovely moment for him. He has strong claims to be in Liverpool’s best XI. Bradley Barcola replaces him, not the player Villarreal’s tired defenders needed to see.

That is surely game over now, Liverpool heading for three Champions League wins from three. Former Newcastle United forward Ayoze Perez is now on for Villarreal. Ngumoha will be replaced by Barcola shortly and I’m sure he will receive a standing ovation.

The game has been transformed, and Villarreal are falling to pieces. They were guilty of losing possession far too cheaply, but Wirtz deserves credit for finishing with an authority he has been accused of lacking. Well struck across the goalkeeper with his left foot, his first Liverpool goal since April.

The floodgates are opening ⚽️ Florian Wirtz scores his first goal of the season for Liverpool 🇩🇪 https://t.co/5HP72tA3bE.

Recent findings suggest that ngumoha has been Liverpool’s best player on the night, although Cardona sold himself all too easily near the touchline. Ngumoha makes the right decision to pick out Mac Allister with a low cross, and the midfielder converts with the simplest of finishes.

Isak then replaces Koumas immediately after the goal.

Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal but Anfield also singing about Rio Ngumoha. He went past two Villarreal defenders to create that one. He has been outstanding.

It has been revealed that there will be time to talk more about Rio Ngumoha – this is his best performance in a Liverpool shirt, a coming-of-age night if you will – but it cannot be overlooked how Alexis Mac Allister has been transformed. He was unrecognisable last season but now he is every inch the man who was a major cog in the push for the title.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

Sources indicate that tsimikas with a dangerous, driven cross from the left which is just beyond the reach of Koumas. Liverpool knocking on the door.

Nyoni’s standing foot was slipping, but he made a clean connection on his shot from range and it whistled just wide of the foot of the post. Ngumoha then has the crowd cooing again, with another drop of the shoulder to beat his man.

Gravenberch found himself sweeping up as Liverpool’s last man, there. The second half has had a more conventional feel, Liverpool making the running as they shoot towards the Kop and their opponents soaking up the pressure. A game of fewer chances since the break.

Always helps having knowledge in close vicinity: a quick discussion with Rafa Benitez about Liverpool’s set up for the second period. Ryan Gravenberch hasn’t been moved to play as a right-back, even though you might think that is the case. Liverpool, essentially, are playing man-against-man. It is going to ask players to be brave on the ball and composed when they are in possession, as the slightest slip will lead to problems. It is high risk and high reward.

Not enough power in Gakpo’s strike from the edge of the area and Gulasci saves. Ngumoha looking such a threat again, attracting the attention of three or four yellow shirts and winning Liverpool another corner. Former Spurs player Juan Foyth has just been introduced by Villarreal.

According to recent reports, liverpool more industrious when they lose possession early in the half. Nyoni then produces a silky turn away from pressure deep in his own half which elicits an “ooohh” from the home fans.

Gravenberch took the ball off Ngumoha’s toes in the box, and the Dutchman’s shot from a tight angle was saved by Gulasci at his near post. I think Ngumoha deserved to have the shot himself after more great skill to find a yard.

Liverpool kick off in the second half.

Wirtz replaces Araujo, which could mean Gravenberch at right-back.

Sources indicate that oluwaseyi, another of Villarreal’s Canadian cohort, is on too. He replaces Saliba.

It has been revealed that florian Wirtz has been readied for action and will soon enter the fray. You would think these will be the kind of conditions in which he will excel. He needs to. Liverpool are lucky to be level.

03:54 - Georges Mikautadze's opener for Villarreal (03:54) is the second-earliest goal Liverpool have conceded at home in major European competition behind only Elpídio Silva's strike in the 3rd minute for Boavista in the UEFA Champions League in September 2001. Cold. https://t.co/NvKmS5jLap.

According to recent reports, dreadful first 30 minutes from Liverpool but they have woken up since, and now they are strong favourites to win the game from here. Iraola’s selection gamble backfired somewhat, but he may well get away with it.

Sources indicate that from the second phase of a corner, Ngumoha did well to keep the ball alive and lift a cross to the back post. Cardona tried to usher the ball behind and made the fatal mistake of letting it bounce in his penalty area, and Araujo sneaked in to score from close range.

It has been revealed that the goalscorer Cardona makes a mistake to let Ngumoha’s cross drift to the backpost. That’s Liverpool’s equaliser from Ronald Araujo. As soon as Liverpool have got their act together they have looked dangerous.

Out of nowhere 😳 Ronald Araújo sneaks in to grab Liverpool's equaliser on the stroke of half-time 🇺🇾 https://t.co/Qrn8PmB2bJ.

The crowd were impatient with him early in the half, but Gakpo is looking more of a threat now, Cruyff-turning away and shooting in the box but Veiga was across to block. Just the one minute of added time to play.

Recent findings suggest that gakpo wins Liverpool a free-kick in a shooting position left of centre, tripped after Nyoni had carried the ball well through midfield. Too much air on the attempt from Mac Allister, who a couple of minutes earlier fired not too far wide from 25 yards.

Plenty for Andoni Iraola to be annoyed about, but as a spectacle this has been far more entertaining than initially assumed.

Really slick interplay from Villarreal again, and Moleiro’s shot from 25 yards is pushed over the bar by Alisson. You can pick holes in Liverpool, but Villarreal’s play deserves plaudits too.

Alexis Mac Allister grabs a goal back for Liverpool 🔴 Game 🔛 https://t.co/Ml9OYgbNq6.

According to recent reports, liverpool have scarcely merited a goal but they have one via a set-piece. Alexis Mac Allister was up early at the near post and he produced a well-directed glancing header into the far corner. That changes the complexion of the game.

It has been revealed that great finish from Mac Allister. The opportunity for Gakpo to cross from the left - that won the corner - was made by Koumas’ hold-up play. First time he has really got hold of it and pinned the defender.

According to recent reports, another run from deep causes Liverpool’s defence problems, but Mikautadze took a touch when a first-time pass could have released the runner through on goal. More groans from the crowd when Tsimikas is caught on the ball.

Then Gakpo flashes a better ball across the face of goal, and Veiga glances it behind for a Liverpool corner.

Industry observers note that villarreal want a corner, and they should have one after a shot deflects off Araujo’s back. Goal kick given though.

Gakpo and Koumas are on the wrong wavelength, and there are groans from the crowd at another misplaced pass.

According to recent reports, liverpool need to dig themselves out of a hole now, Villarreal have cut them apart to score a simple second. Cardona, the left-back, with a run from deep, and Tsimikas was playing him onside. Cardona had all the time in the world to steady himself and roll the ball beyond Alisson.

According to recent reports, defensive calamity for Liverpool. Both Mikautadze and Cardona could have taken that through ball from Saliba and finished.

Straight through the heart of the defence 👀 Sergi Cardona doubles Villarreal's lead at Anfield 🤯 https://t.co/ZPHAkiLjN0.

Industry observers note that liverpool far too easy to play through at the moment, Villarreal might not be an elite team but they have enough technique to pass and move well if given the time. Mikautadze lacks some pace up front, but has shown some silky touches. As Alan Shearer puts in on Amazon Prime: “Feels like a training match for Liverpool. So lazy. Where’s the urgency?”.

Better from Liverpool with Nyoni driving forward and the ball almost running into the path of Gravenberch for a strike from the edge of the box. Villarreal diligent in their defensive work though, no clear sight of goal for the Liverpool players so far.

According to recent reports, anyone who is experiencing Anfield on a European night for the first time will be wondering what all the fuss is about. Aside from a couple of flurries following a Ronald Araujo tackle and a Rio Ngumoha dribble, it has been deathly quiet. Rafael Benitez, an architect of some of the wildest evenings here, is in the press box alongside Robbie Fowler and they are a reminder of how it used to be. Liverpool need to raise themselves to bring the crowd to life.

According to recent reports, ngumoha is the one ray of light for Liverpool so far, he has the beating of Villarreal left-back Cardona whenever he drops a shoulder. Gulasci palms his deflected cross over and Villarreal survive the corner.

Industry observers note that the flag was eventually raised for offside, but Villarreal were in behind the Liverpool defence again after a misplaced Van Dijk pass. Liverpool have not got themselves out of the blocks at all. They have lost possession too cheaply and look vulnerable defensively.

Buchanan with a teasing low cross through the Liverpool penalty area, and the winger is justified when looking quizzically at his team-mates. If one of the yellow shirts had gambled they would have had a tap in.

Most of Liverpool’s attacks are being funnelled down their right so far, perhaps no surprise given that is where Ngumoha is stationed. Liverpool yet to test the goalkeeper, though.

Industry observers note that villarreal then throw a punch of their own down the other end, with Saliba turning and shooting at the edge of the box. Deflected, and Villarreal have a corner. Delivery is poor and Liverpool clear.

The Spanish team are moving the ball around with assurance, some nice touches from Saliba in their midfield (the Canada international is no relation to the Arsenal centre-back).

Sources indicate that hats off to Villarreal coach Inigo Perez, who is not wearing a hat or, indeed, a coat. Instead he is steadfastly ignoring the cold drizzle and treating this, from a touchline outfit point of view, like a warm summer’s evening on the Valencian coast. Polo shirt and slacks for the young Spanish coach.

No need for Liverpool to panic just yet, plenty of time to turn this around, and Rio Ngumoha is going the right way about it. Quick feet in the box to beat his man and fashion a yard for a strike, but his shot is blocked. Ngumoha is playing on Liverpool’s right tonight with Gakpo on the opposite flank.

What a remarkable start. Virgil van Dijk has looked a gear or two behind everyone in the opening stages. One bad touch required Jeremy Jacquet to make a swift recovery and that misplaced header has now handed Villarreal the lead. Social media will be abuzz with scrutiny about Van Dijk now, as is always the case when he errs, but it won’t be taken into consideration that he has been one of Liverpool’s best players in these opening 10 games. What price would you make him to atone with a header at the other end later in the game?

Van Dijk has made two dreadful mistakes in the first four minutes and this time he is punished. Liverpool’s captain was trying to guide a header back to Alisson, but the ball shanked off his forehead at the wrong angle and dropped for Mikautadze in the box. The striker was free, and he finished well across Alisson. That was not in the script.

The Georgian No 9 for Villarreal Georges Mikautadze had looked so lightweight in the early duels with Virgil Van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet. They had muscled him off the ball more than once. That was a gift from Van Dijk and Mikautadze took it very well.

Ryan Gravenberch has started the game in a more advanced midfield role with Nyoni and Mac Allister behind him. The home team are yet to string together a serious sequence of passes in the Villarreal half.

Villarreal get the game under way.

It’s another young Liverpool team fielded in the Champions League, but they should have enough about them to see off this Villarreal side.

Different circumstances. It’s out fourth game in 10 days, Florian [Wirtz] and Bradley [Barcola] have played almost every minute so we have to be sensible and the same with Alex [Isak].

I think he is doing very well [Leiws Koumas], or else we would not trust him to start these kinds of games.

Probably difficult to find someone who knows me better [than Inigo Perez], but we also know him!

Subs: Junior, Costa, Freeman, Diatta, Gerard, Foyth, Akhomach, Macia, Oluwaseyi, Perez, El Jmili, Gaitan Diaz.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Nyoni, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Barcola, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Laffey.

A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

Iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Industry observers note that your Reds to take on Villarreal in the #UCL! 🔴💫 https://t.co/tlQNFZVMBv.

The club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Industry observers note that dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

It has been revealed that liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

Sources indicate that they have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 37 min read (7390 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

The scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data generated for this study are available from the GEO under accessions GSE306808 and GSE347564, respectively. Sequencing reads were aligned to the GRCh38 human reference genome (10x Genomics GRCh38-2020 for scRNA-seq; Ensembl GRCh38, assembly accession GCA_000001405.29, for bulk RNA-seq). Previously published29 human embryo scRNA-seq data are available from the GEO under accession GSE155121. Other reanalysed datasets are available from the following repositories: mouse gastrulation, ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-6967)55; cynomolgus macaque embryo, GEO (GSE193007)56; RA-gastruloid, GEO (GSE208369)57; axial organoid, GEO (GSE220563)17; axioloid, GEO (GSE199576)18; and segmentoid, GEO (GSE195467)19. GEO series are accessible at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ and ArrayExpress experiments at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress. The confocal and time-lapse datasets are large multichannel image series that are impractical to deposit in full; the measurement tables from which the quantitative imaging panels are plotted are provided in the code repository (Code availability). Raw imaging data, and any additional information required to reanalyse the data reported in this study, are available from the lead contact, S.R., on request; requests will be answered within 1 month and data shared by secure electronic file transfer without restriction. Source data are provided with this paper.

Sources indicate that custom code for image analysis and for bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq analysis—including SMD feature selection, clustering and annotation, and the trunk morph–embryo correspondence analyses—is available under the MIT License at GitHub (https://github.com/stevenzwick/zwick-2026-trunk-morphogenesis) and archived at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22756590)58. Random seeds and exact parameters (intensity thresholds and gates, background offsets, local-threshold window sizes, Gaussian σ, histogram edges, clustering resolutions and curated gene lists) are provided in the repository.

It has been revealed that a, A detailed schematic of the workflow is shown: (i) Matrigel is microcontact printed onto the two-layered PDMS stamp (PDMS-ii) using a flat PDMS stamp (PDMS-i). (ii) A thin PDMS microwell array is peeled from the silicon master and overlaid on a glass coverslip. Taller PDMS sidewalls are plasma-bonded along two edges. (iii) Capillary water flow through the microchannels drives localized Matrigel transfer from stamp PDMS-ii onto the PDMS microwell layer at the contact interface. (iv) Cells are seeded onto the transferred Matrigel pattern, overlaid with a silanized coverslip atop the sidewalls, and cultured further with media and microwell-trapped beads. b, Photographs of the experimental setup corresponding to steps a(i–iii): coating the flat stamp (grey border, fourth column, top); PDMS-ii stamps with different patterns (blue border, first column); PDMS microwell layer with wells at different positions (red border, second column); aligned PDMS-ii stamp and PDMS microwell layer in contact (green border, third column); and the application of weight and water flow for transfer (green border, fourth column, bottom). MG, Matrigel; RT, room temperature.

Recent findings suggest that a–d, Design of two-layer PDMS stamp and microwell substrate: a, upper-layer pattern used to print Matrigel features; b, lower-layer embedded microchannels (white denotes channel features); c, assembled two-layer PDMS stamp with a three-dimensional illustration of the assembled stamp below; d, alignment of stamp features and microwell layer, with 120 µm diameter microwells positioned at defined distances from pattern edges. Scale bars, 1 mm. e, Whole-chip images show humidified microcontact printing (HµCP) of Matrigel mixed with fluorescently conjugated BSA (cyan) onto PDMS microwell chip (brightfield, grey), using a four-square stamp pattern. Air bubbles beneath PDMS microwell layer and above glass coverslip are visible in brightfield images. Images are representative of 6 independent experiments (12 chips) with similar results. Scale bars, 1 mm. f, Whole-chip image shows standard microcontact printing (µCP) of fluorescent BSA onto glass to validate stamp pattern from a. Image is representative of 2 independent experiments (5 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. g, Image shows pluripotent epithelial cysts formed 3 days after seeding on a PDMS microwell chip, using stamp pattern from a. A diversity of cyst arrangements, rather than the optimized hexagonal pattern with a central cyst as in Fig. 1, are used to show the flexibility of the approach. Image is representative of 79 independent experiments (145 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. h, Whole-chip epifluorescence image shows pluripotent cysts (DAPI, grey), well-trapped BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence (pSMAD, green) 6 h after bead deposition. Image is representative of 6 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. i, Representative higher magnification images of cyst arrays with adjacent BMP beads and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence 6 h after bead deposition, from three independent experiments. (Top row) Five-cyst arrays with one or two beads, from chip in h. (Bottom left) Seven-cyst array with two beads, from an independent experiment. (Bottom right) Five-cyst array with three beads, from an independent experiment. Scale bars, 100 µm. j, (Left) Plot shows normalized pSMAD1/5/9 intensity (pSMAD/DAPI) versus distance from BMP bead, d, for all cysts from chip in h except cysts at centre of arrays (n = 201 cysts; light grey lines, individual cyst profiles; solid lines, mean; shaded areas, ±1 s.d.). (Right) pSMAD1/5/9 intensity in the bead-proximal epithelium of each cyst is plotted against the distance to the nearest bead, dmin, showing a negative correlation (red line, R2 = 0.624; n = 156 cysts) up to a distance of 635 µm, beyond which the intensity is low and uncorrelated (R2 = 0.061; n = 45 cysts). k, (Left) Normalized pSMAD1/5/9 is plotted against angle relative to bead direction (θ - θb) for cysts within responsive regime (d < 635 µm; n = 156 cysts). (Right) The direction of the pSMAD1/5/9 distribution, quantified by its first moment, is plotted as a function of the angle towards the nearest bead, θb (R2 = 0.17, n = 156 cysts). The correlation between pSMAD1/5/9 direction and bead angle is weaker than in Fig. 1f due to the overlapping influence of multiple BMP beads positioned near most cyst arrays in h.

a, (top) Live YFP and merged Brightfield (BF)–YFP images show hexagonally arranged cysts derived from the BMP4-T2A-Achilles reporter hPSC line 6 h after exposure to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), with no detectable YFP signal. Images are from one experiment (36 cyst arrays). (bottom) Live images of the cysts from (top) 24 h after bead exposure show the presence of YFP (arrowhead) in some cells adjacent to beads. Images are from one experiment (2 cyst arrays). b, Plot of BMP4 read counts per million (CPM) from bulk RNA sequencing of pluripotent cysts at 0 h, 7 h, and 24 h after BMP bead exposure (n = 3 biologically independent samples per timepoint). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. BMP5 expression was not detected in any of the samples. c, (left) Brightfield, DAPI (grey) and definitive endoderm marker SOX17 immunofluorescence (cyan) images show spatially arranged cysts after a 2-day exposure to the main experimental conditions, including BMP bead exposure, WNT-driven symmetry breaking, and Activin/Nodal signalling inhibitor A83-01 (above), or without A83-01 (below). Images are from one experiment per condition (with A83-01: 1 chip, 21 cyst arrays; without A83-01: 2 chips, 47 cyst arrays). (right) Bulk RNA-seq analysis of key endodermal genes in cysts under the same two conditions, with (green, n = 3 biologically independent samples) or without A83-01 (purple, n = 2 biologically independent samples). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. A83-01 prevents endoderm differentiation in all protocols here (Extended Data Fig. 5b, Fig. 4, Supplementary Data 5). d, (left) Plot of DAPI-normalized SOX2 and TBXT intensity versus distance from central cyst of array (“anterior”). TBXT varies more with distance from anterior than distance from bead (Fig. 2c) due to A–P symmetry breaking from geometric cyst arrangement16,17 (Fig. 1b). Black arrow indicates the regime where both TBXT and SOX2 are high, corresponding to NMP differentiation (n = 210 biologically independent cysts; thin lines, individual cyst profiles; thick line, mean; shaded area, 95% confidence interval). (right) Pixel density plot of normalized SOX2 versus TBXT; percentages, fractions of pixels above and below the cutoffs. 28% of pixels are SOX2+ TBXT+, indicative of NMP-like expression. e, Brightfield, DAPI (grey), and TBXT immunofluorescence (cyan) images of three hexagonal cyst arrays without (left) or with a central cyst (right) on the same chip. In the absence of the central cyst, hexagonal cysts are prone to express TBXT on both their inward- and outward-facing poles (white arrowheads), indicating a lack of clear A-P polarity. With the central cyst present, TBXT expression is restricted to the outward-facing pole. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (12 cyst arrays) with similar results. f, Brightfield and immunofluorescence images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent lateral plate mesoderm (LPM, red) proximal to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red; red arrows top left, white arrows elsewhere), whereas FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm (magenta) and SOX2+ neural progenitors (yellow) are distant from beads. Cysts are from another chip of the same design (Extended Data Fig. 2a). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments with similar results. g, Pixel-density plots of FOXA2 versus FOXF1 (top) and SOX2 versus FOXF1 (bottom) immunofluorescence in day 2 cysts, indicating mutual exclusivity. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to the 99th percentile of bin density; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines; dashed lines, positivity thresholds; percentages, fraction of pixels in each quadrant. n = 7 biologically independent cysts from 3 independent experiments. h, Images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent LPM located proximally to BMP beads, FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm distant from beads, and TBXT+ mesoderm at posterior end of cysts. Images are representative of 5 independent experiments with similar results. i, Per-chip fraction of cysts containing FOXF1:Achilles+ cells, plotted as in Fig. 2e, for each condition: adjacent to a BMP bead (“Bead”), no bead (“No Bead”) and adjacent to a bead following BMPR1A knockdown (“KD”). Dots, one chip from each of four independent experiments; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. across experiments. n = 182 (“Bead”), 1,010 (“No Bead”) and 189 (“KD”) cysts scored in total (see Methods, “Fraction of FOXF1+ cysts”). j, BMPR1A CPM from bulk RNA-seq of cells following BMPR1A knockdown compared with a scrambled control (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. Two-sided Welch’s t-test: t = −7.00, d.f. = 2.5, P = 0.010, mean difference −28.1 CPM (95% CI, −42.3 to −13.9). *P < 0.05. k, Quantification of pSMAD1/5/9 in cells at the edge following 30 min treatment with 10 ng ml−1 BMP4. BMPR1A knockdown cells show reduced pSMAD1/5/9 compared with SCRAMBLE control cells (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Additional quantification at different time points and cell locations is provided in Supplementary Data 4. Dots, per-well medians; centre line, median; boxes, interquartile range; whiskers, extreme values within 1.5× interquartile range. l, Representative immunostaining images for the analysis in k: BMPR1A knockdown (top row) and SCRAMBLE (bottom row); knockdown cells (CFP, yellow, left), DAPI (middle), and pSMAD1/5/9 (cyan, right). Images are from one experiment (3 wells each). m, Images show two additional replicates of day 2 morphs as in Fig. 2f, showing the co-expression of BMP4:Achilles (green) and FOXF1:mScarlet3 (red). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. n, Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for BMP4 (green) and FOXF1 (red) transcripts show co-localization in a bead-adjacent cyst after 2 days of differentiation. Representative image from n = 6 biologically independent bead-adjacent cysts. o, Pixel-density plot of FOXF1 versus BMP4 in situ signal in the day 2 cyst shown in n. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to its maximum; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines. The two signals are positively correlated (R2 = 0.646). Scale bars, 100 µm.

a, A schematic of trunk morph differentiation protocol is shown. hPSCs were seeded onto micropatterned PDMS microwell substrate on Day −3 in mTeSR Plus with 10 µM Y-27632. The next day, Y-27632 was removed from media conditions and Matrigel added to induce the formation of single lumen epithelial cysts. On Day 0, BMP4-coated beads were injected into microwells, and cyst differentiation was initiated in N2B27 with 8–10 µM CHIR99021, 0.1–0.15 µM A83-01, and 50 ng ml−1 NOGGIN. After 48 h, cysts were transferred to individual wells in N2B27 with Matrigel and cultured for 3–4 days before analysis. b, Box-and-whisker plots show length of trunk morphs at 0, 48, and 120 h of differentiation. The same n = 93 biologically independent trunk morph samples were tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. c, (left) Box-and-whisker plots of trunk morph length on days 3, 4 and 5 without (red, n = 10 biologically independent trunk morph samples) or with the WNT-secretion inhibitor IWP3 (green, n = 8 biologically independent trunk morph samples), added after 48 h; each morph was tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. Differences between conditions at each time point were assessed using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons; Hodges-Lehmann median differences are given with Bonferroni-adjusted (98.3%) confidence intervals. Day 3: U = 16, P = 0.103, −59 µm (−160 to 18). Day 4: U = 4, P = 1.6 × 10−3, −212 µm (−314 to −100). Day 5: U = 0, P = 1.4 × 10−4, −353 µm (−438 to −287). ns, P > 0.05; **, P < 0.01; ***, P < 0.001. (Right) Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for WNT3A (left, green) and WNT5A (right, magenta) transcripts, together with brightfield imaging, show WNT ligand expression at the posterior end (n = 5 biologically independent trunk morph samples per probe, from 2 independent experiments). d, Representative epifluorescence images of trunk morphs after transient BMP4-bead exposure show FOXF1+ lateral plate mesoderm (cyan) bilaterally (left), unilaterally (middle), and posteriorly localized (right). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (11 chips, 93 trunk morphs scored across all bead configurations) with similar results. e, Representative images of day 5 trunk morphs following transient exposure to medially positioned BMP4-coated beads. Posterior-restricted LPM was observed only at bead-cyst distances below 160 µm (5 of 12 morphs); all 9 trunk morphs with larger distances revealed bilateral FOXF1. Images are from one experiment (3 chips, 21 trunk morphs). f-g, Representative images of trunk morphs exposed to (f) a unilateral bead or (g) two bilateral beads show unilateral or bilateral FOXF1, respectively. MESP2:mCherry is bilateral in all morphs. Images are representative of the same experiments and morphs as in d. h, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), MESP2:mCherry (red), phalloidin (grey), and FOXF1 (cyan) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible within the single focal plane. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (2 trunk morphs) with similar results. i, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), phalloidin (grey), FOXC1 (cyan), and MESP2:mCherry (red) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible within the single focal plane. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (4 trunk morphs) with similar results. j, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), phalloidin (grey), PAX3 (red), and SOX2 (yellow) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible in a 30-µm z-projection. Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (7 trunk morphs) with similar results. k, Confocal images at different z-planes (z = 330, 380, and 745 µm from the base) of trunk morph in Fig. 3h show DAPI (grey), FOXF1 (cyan), and MESP2:mCherry (red). As in many trunk morphs, somites (white arrows) are visible at specific confocal planes but are not apparent in the maximum z-projection shown in Fig. 3h. Scale bar, 100 µm.

Recent findings suggest that a, Confocal images of day 5 trunk morphs with medial bead (left) or unilateral bead exposure (right) show DAPI (grey), MESP2:mCherry (red; paraxial mesoderm), PAX8 (yellow; intermediate mesoderm), and FOXF1:Achilles (cyan; LPM), along with inset images of lateral region at higher magnification. Images are representative of 10 independent experiments (55 trunk morphs) with similar results. b, Epifluorescence images of day 5 trunk morphs without beads (left, three morphs; brightfield) or with a medial bead (right; DAPI, grey) show MESP2:mCherry (red; paraxial mesoderm), FOXA2 (green; axial mesoderm) and no SOX17 (magenta; endoderm). FOXA2+ cells are present in all morphs but fewer in morphs exposed to bead. Yellow outlines mark the boundary to which images were cropped for display (see Methods, “Image display”). Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (3 chips) with similar results. c, Epifluorescence (left, right) and confocal (middle) images of day 5 trunk morphs exposed to BMP4-coated beads in three configurations: medial (left), unilateral (middle), and bilateral (right). FOXF1 (cyan) appears unilaterally or bilaterally reflecting bead geometry, whereas MESP2:mCherry (red) is bilateral in all conditions. FOXA2 is confined to medial regions and diminished relative to no-bead controls in b. Images are representative of 8 independent experiments with similar results. Scale bars, 100 µm.

a, Hierarchically clustered single-cell gene expression matrices of stem cell-based trunk morphs after 6 days of differentiation, without and with BMP bead exposure, are shown. Each column represents an individual cell, rows correspond to key genes, and matrix values show normalized gene expression as indicated by the colour scale. Cluster annotations are indicated by the colour bar and legend (right). n = 2,748 cells without beads; 2,558 cells with beads. b, UMAP plots of single-cell transcriptomes from day 6 trunk morphs are shown as in Fig. 4b, coloured by BMP bead exposure history (left) and by cluster identity (right). c, Ordered list of gene panel used in a and in Fig. 4d,e. Genes were manually chosen and assigned as cluster-representative by comparing differentially expressed genes against established cell type markers from literature. d, Hierarchically clustered single-cell gene expression matrices from trunk morphs, without and with BMP bead exposure, are shown. Rows correspond to top five differentially expressed genes for each cluster as identified by multinomial logistic regression analysis.

It has been revealed that a, (Left) Hierarchically subclustered single-cell gene expression matrices are shown for cells originally assigned to somite clusters (“Early Somite”, “Mature Somite”) from trunk morphs without and with BMP bead exposure (see Supplementary Data 1, 5). Sub-cluster annotations are indicated by colour bar and legend below. n = 825 cells without beads; n = 129 cells with beads. (Top right) UMAP plots of 954 somite cell transcriptomes from trunk morphs without or with BMP bead exposure are shown, coloured by subcluster identity. (Bottom right) Stacked bar graphs show the fraction of each somite subcluster among somite cells from trunk morphs, without and with BMP bead exposure. b, Same as a, but for hierarchical subclustering of “Forebrain/Midbrain” cluster. n = 283 cells without beads; n = 263 cells with beads. c, Same as a but for cells from LPM and intermediate mesoderm (IM) clusters from BMP bead–exposed trunk morphs, revealing three distinct subpopulations: endothelial progenitors, cardiac-biased anterior trunk LPM, and posterior trunk LPM. Rows correspond to key differentially expressed marker genes. d, (Top) Images show brightfield, MESP2:mCherry (red), and FOXF1:Achilles (YFP, cyan) in a live day 8 trunk morph pre-fixation. By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 12:02.

Sources indicate that donyell Malen has been a new man since arriving at Roma. With the Dutch striker the top league scorer in Europe's big five leagues in 2026, can he join one of Europe's best clubs?

It has been revealed that struggling at Aston Villa, Malen joined Roma in January 2026 on a £1.7m (€2m) loan. The Dutch striker has stepped up a level since moving to the Italian capital, and he is enjoying an exceptional 2026 calendar year with 26 league goals.

Industry observers note that that makes him the top scorer across Europe's five biggest leagues over that period, ahead of Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe (21 goals). His current success has not gone unnoticed and led Roma to invest £21.3m (€25m) to sign the best recruit of 2026 permanently.

Industry observers note that malen has not been affected by the permanent transfer and is continuing on excellent foundations at the start of the season. He now has 12 goals in 11 Serie A matches, and must also add five goals and two assists in five Champions League matches.

The versatile forward, who was often used on the flanks at Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa, has been installed as the number nine by Gian Piero Gasperini with great success.

The Dutchman's performances are logically starting to attract more prestigious suitors.

With Kane injured at Bayern Munich and Doue and Kvaratskhelia injured at PSG, Malen's name has been cited as a target for both giants.

According to recent reports, the two-time European champions are looking for a versatile forward for January, which is exactly what Malen is. His profile fits Paris's needs.

However, PSG do not want to overpay, and as things stand Roma have no interest in selling their star man, who is under contract until June 2030, in the middle of the season unless an exceptional offer arrives. A transfer in January therefore looks very unlikely, even to Bayern Munich, where he would also make a lot of sense with Kane absent for several months.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, if Malen continues in this vein, the approaches should multiply next summer. A move to one of Europe's heavyweights could also appeal to the Roma forward, with the Italian club potentially struggling to keep hold of him and to turn down huge offers.

Florian Wirtz has thanked Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola for sparking his resurgence and insists he never stopped believing in himself.

The German arrived with a massive reputation when he completed a £116million move from Bayer Leverkusen but has been a constant punchbag for critics after failing to reach the heights that saw him win the Bundesliga title as the league’s star man.

Wirtz, though, has been much improved this year and put in his best performance for the Reds on Sunday in the 4-0 thumping of Manchester United And he insists Iraola – and old Anfield boss Jurgen Klopp – are the reason.

It has been revealed that ‘I am really enjoying playing under him,’ stated Wirtz on Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer. ‘He is a really good coach. He has shown that his whole career as a manager.

‘He is bringing me back to the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football.

Industry observers note that ‘I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me. I am really happy with that.’.

Florian Wirtz has opened up on talking to ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp after finally hitting form for Liverpool.

Wirtz won man of the match in Liverpool's 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United on Sunday.

In a recent development, wirtz has also had the added influence of Klopp, now Germany boss, in recent months. He said: ‘We always speak about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He is the coach who stayed here the most of his career.

‘He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to get successful over here because he has shown how it is done.

'He knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here, he can give me some good advice.’.

Industry observers note that wirtz added: ‘It's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself.

‘I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities and I know them now. Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I'm just enjoying the moment and really happy at the moment that it's going well. I'm happy with myself.’.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Cody Gakpo will miss the Merseyside derby with a calf problem and fellow Dutchman Ryan Gravenberch is also in a race against time to be fit for the trip to Everton due to a fascia glitch. Neither have travelled to Belgium for Liverpool’s clash against Club Brugge.

#130158. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one issue ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

Recent findings suggest that with Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already mentioned he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, stated in a note.

Industry observers note that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Recent findings suggest that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, stated the vote demonstrated the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of big tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

Sources indicate that "This election highlights that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he mentioned. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

Industry observers note that if the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown noted, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

Industry observers note that that sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

Industry observers note that "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

Trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard remarked, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump stated in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election matter — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

In a recent development, "You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most vital thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he said in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and issues.

Industry observers note that yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another problem vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the newly introduced Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard said. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

The additions of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and more recently Jeremy Jacquet and Luca Brughmans are proof of the philosophy in place within Liverpool's recruitment team.

With Julian Ward at the helm, the recruitment strategy doesn't seem to have changed, and the Reds continue to be linked with some of the most promising young talents from across Europe and beyond.

Liverpool's mission remains the same but that doesn't mean that they are automatically the favourites for every wonderkid, and they appear to be falling behind in the race for one highly rated defender.

  • Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that mentioned, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo.

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis.

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Julian Ward and Andoni Iraola have a lot of work to do on Liverpool's first-team squad this January.

Over £150 million was already spent on the club this summer but, since they're presently fourth in the table and find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal, they have a bit of ground to make up.

Obviously, all of their problems can't be rectified in the winter window but, if they can fix some of their main ones, that would be spectacular.

Not only would bringing in another player or two give the Reds a boost but, it would also help them get back on track and start to get back to their best.

Liverpool see Gustavo Varela as a 'long-term target' rather than a short-term option.

Over the last few days, the transfer rumour mill has been going into overdrive.

Every single position among the Reds ranks is being scrutinised with fans seemingly rather happy with the recent performances of their club.

On Sunday, they managed to beat Manchester United 4-0 and, even though the Red Devils were down to 10 men for most of the day, Liverpool's performance was still impressive.

However, their problem areas were made clear once again with only two strikers available for Iraola to choose from.

And, of the two, one of them was Lewis Koumas who, even though he's good, he doesn't really jump out as a Premier League-winning attacker.

Because of this, rumours about the future of Liverpool's attack have emerged with Monza's Gustavo Varela now appearing on the Reds' shortlist.

However, a recent report from Football Insider has clarified just how serious Liverpool are about bringing the Portuguese striker in.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

"The 21-year-old has emerged as a target for the Reds, having struck 11 goals from his opening 11 games in Serie A so far this term.

"The Reds are "keeping tabs" on the Portuguese youngster, with several top Italian clubs also having their "eyes fixed on him" at the moment.

"However, sources say that Varela is viewed as more of a long-term option at Anfield, and the club are not likely to make a move for him this winter.

"Monza are relaxed over their frontman's future for now, but they know that further interest from top clubs is inevitable if he continues to perform.".

Gustavo Varela is an interesting transfer for Liverpool to explore.

Varela is almost certainly a player that barely anyone outside of Italy will have heard of.

The Portuguese striker is the Serie A's current top goal scorer despite his team being in a relegation battle.

The strangest thing is that, he only just joined the Italian outfit during the 2026-27 summer transfer window for €2.5 million.

Before this term, he'd had a couple of poor seasons but now, he really seems to have come into his own despite only being 21 years old.

His age coupled with his keen eye for goal are two major boxes that Liverpool like to tick when looking for attackers and, if the fee that Monza want is reasonable, there's no reason why a deal couldn't be explored.

Obviously, there's no point going for him in January as, the Reds need to see how good Hugo Ekitike is first but, as a potential option for the future, Varela looks like a fairly solid option.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:42 EST, 24 November 2026.

Derek McInnes last night hit out at his dozy Rangers side for switching off in the latter stages of a hard-fought 3-2 home win over Aberdeen and warned them they will be made to pay over the course of the season if they carry on being so naive.

Goals from Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Raskin in the first ten minutes of the second half put the Ibrox outfit in total command after Brad Lyons had put the visitors a goal up at the break.

However, Findlay Marshall made it a nervy finish for Rangers after scoring for the Dons on 58 minutes and it took a brilliant save from keeper Ivor Pandur to deny Nicky Devlin before Rangers saw it out to take their unbeaten run to 14 games and close the gap on Celtic at the head of the Premiership to just one point.

It has been revealed that ‘I am relieved to win,’ noted manager McInnes, who made three changes and altered the shape at the interval. ‘I thought we only played with the intelligence, speed and intensity for about 20 minutes and, in that period, showed how good we can be.

It has been revealed that ‘But we put the game at risk. We lost a cheap goal and weren’t aggressive enough. We lost two goals, really, from set-plays.

‘At 3-1 up against a team as game as Aberdeen were — and they were really good value — our naivety for the second goal is beyond me.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes was relieved to win but urges his side to keep focused.

Nicolas Raskin slots home the third goal for Rangers in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen.

‘I am not sure it was a free-kick in the first place, but we turn our backs. It is almost as if we are in a daydream and we allow them to manipulate the ball. Great finish from wee Findlay Marshall, but we put ourselves in the mire there by just knocking off.

According to recent reports, ‘We were so naive at times in the game. We scored good goals at good times but I still think Aberdeen will be disappointed not to get something.

‘We should have stayed in charge of the game and the second goal we lose allows Aberdeen to keep going with a bit of oxygen and carry a threat. I am disappointed with the lack of control in the game and I am not really happy with a lot of what we saw.

‘That has to change because we will not always be able to outscore the opposition.

In a recent development, ‘We hit Aberdeen like a train in the second half and they found themselves 3-1 down because of the quality and intelligence of our play. For whatever reason, we then started playing back the way again. We played more passbacks to my goalkeeper than I can remember in a long time.

Industry observers note that ‘We need to play forward and show more control in the game. I am looking for better from my team.’.

Raskin, meanwhile, has urged his Rangers team-mates to blast themselves to the top of the table on Saturday night and really pile the pressure on arch-rivals Celtic.

The Light Blues play host to third-placed Falkirk on Saturday afternoon with Celtic going to Hearts the following day and the Belgian midfielder wants to make sure they don’t let the defending champions off the hook the way they have in previous years.

According to recent reports, ‘We need to keep it going,’ noted Raskin. ‘In recent years, we have not been able to put enough pressure on the other team and now we are doing it, so that is good.

‘We will see how everybody reacts after next Saturday.’.

Djeidi Gassama scored to complete a stunning turaround for Rangers early in the second half.

Raskin has also revealed it took a stern half-time team talk from manager McInnes along with those substitutions to spark his side into life after a dreadful first-half performance.

According to recent reports, ‘I think we made the game hard for ourselves in the first half,’ said the Belgian. ‘The manager had an honest discussion in the dressing room and we came back and scored two early goals, which helped. But we weren’t focused enough after the third goal and conceded to make it even harder.

Sources indicate that ‘We indicated character again. The manager said what a manager has to say when you are losing, playing badly, you are 1-0 down and you have to win the game.’.

Aberdeen boss Mario Frick left Ibrox feeling his side had missed a real opportunity.

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an key victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts currently sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

Wael Mohya has swiftly become one of the most exciting young talents in world football.

Liverpool have been repeatedly linked with the teenager in recent weeks, and now Brighton are reportedly ready to challenge the Reds for the 17-year-old's signature.

A summer deal seems the most likely for the 17-year-old, but Liverpool should start laying the groundwork now to get ahead of Brighton.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No.
  • "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

According to recent reports, "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo noted in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

While his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and stated he wouldn't start the next one.

According to recent reports, ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

#130147. Latest Update: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

Latest Update: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

Opinion: Andoni Iraola will start 'outstanding' attacker vs Club Brugge

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (498 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool have performed much better since they were beaten by Fenerbahce in the Champions League a few weeks ago.
  • The Reds were torn apart by the Turkish Super Lig outfit with former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt leading his team to a historic win.
  • Indeed, they are one of the better teams in Turkey but, compared to how much talent the Reds have among their ranks, they shouldn't have even had a chance to beat them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have performed much better since they were beaten by Fenerbahce in the Champions League a few weeks ago.

The Reds were torn apart by the Turkish Super Lig outfit with former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt leading his team to a historic win.

Indeed, they are one of the better teams in Turkey but, compared to how much talent the Reds have among their ranks, they shouldn't have even had a chance to beat them.

That's why Liverpool's defeat was so hard to take for fans.

However, as mentioned, since then, things have gone well for Liverpool with the club even beating arch-rivals Manchester United 4-0.

Even though transfers are expected to occur in the January transfer window, Andoni Iraola still has a few players among his ranks who fans haven't seen the best of yet.

That's why Wednesday's Champions League tie against Club Brugge could be incredibly crucial for one of them.

Victor Munoz has to start against Club Brugge.

Sunday's game was Liverpool's highlight of the season so far.

Their win against the Red Devils meant that they were thrusted back into fourth position and now find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

This is still a decent gap to cut down but, it's a lot less daunting than the nine points that separated them over the international break.

During Sunday's victory against Man United, Victor Munoz was left on the bench to start with.

And, even though Liverpool were winning their arch-rivals 3-0 when the last 20 minutes of the game came upon them, Iraola still chose to bring the Spaniard on.

Most people expected that transfer to have been done to give those who started a rest but, Munoz had other prepares.

In the 18 minutes of football that he played, his lightning quick speed and his ability to turn nothing chances into goals paid off as the 23-year-old bagged the Reds' fourth and last goal of the game.

He also maintained a 92 per cent pass accuracy and he even made one key pass.

This performance alone proves why he should be starting against Club Brugge in Liverpool's next Champions League tie.

Victor Munoz could become a key player for Liverpool in the next couple of years.

Munoz was Liverpool's bargain signing of the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard was brought in by the Reds for a fee worth around £35 million.

At the time, Newcastle were also trying to sign him but, in the end, he chose Liverpool.

Most fans thought that he'd be more of a back-up than anything else but, in reality, he's become a key member of Iraola's first-team squad.

His performances have been second to none and, even though he's often been used in his less preferred position of right-wing, he's still contributed to four goals in the 13 games he's featured in.

Here's hoping that, if Iraola does start the "outstanding" attacker on Wednesday, that he can put on another stellar performance.
